findings.title: Unrelated audit log changes introduce crashes on null member and incompatible paginator
findings.body:
`OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint.get` adds an unrelated `optimized_pagination=true` branch that has multiple defects:

1. `organization_context.member` can be `None` (for example, when a superuser who is not a member of the organization accesses the endpoint), so `organization_context.member.has_global_access` raises `AttributeError` whenever `request.user.is_superuser` is false.
2. `self.paginate(...)` is passed `paginator_cls=OptimizedCursorPaginator` with `order_by="-datetime"`. `AuditLogEntry.datetime` is a `datetime` object, and `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key` calls `math.floor(value)` / `math.ceil(value)` directly on the `datetime` attribute (unlike `DateTimePaginator`), raising `TypeError: must be real number, not datetime.datetime`. Similarly, `value_from_cursor` returns the raw numeric cursor value instead of converting it to a `datetime` for the SQL comparison.

These changes to `organization_auditlogs.py`, `paginator.py`, and `cursors.py` are also completely unrelated to the PR's stated purpose of optimizing span buffer insertion.

findings.title: Negative cursor offsets passed to Django QuerySet slicing raise ValueError
findings.body: In `BasePaginator.get_result` (line 182) and `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result` (lines 880-886), negative `cursor.offset` values are preserved in `start_offset` (when `cursor.is_prev` is true or `enable_advanced_features` is enabled) and passed directly to `queryset[start_offset:stop]`. Django `QuerySet` slicing does not support negative indices and raises `ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported.` whenever `start_offset < 0` or `stop < 0`, turning a user-supplied cursor parameter into an unhandled 500 error. In addition, line 192 (`len(results) == offset + limit + extra`) still uses `offset` instead of `start_offset`.

findings.title: Span eviction deletes redirect entries only on flush, leaking redirects for evicted spans
findings.body: `add-buffer.lua` now evicts spans with the smallest `end_timestamp_precise` via `redis.call("zpopmin", set_key, span_count - 1000)` when a segment exceeds 1000 spans, and can even evict the segment's root span if it finished earlier than child spans. However, `done_flush_segments` in `src/sentry/spans/buffer.py` only removes entries from the redirect hash (`span-buf:sr:{project_id:trace_id}`) for spans that were still present in the segment when flushed. Any span evicted by `zpopmin` never has its redirect entry cleaned up by `hdel`, leaving stale redirects until the entire hash expires.

findings.title: `max_segment_spans` parameter on `SpansBuffer` is now unused and inconsistent with Lua limit
findings.body: `SpansBuffer.__init__` still accepts `max_segment_spans: int = 1001` and stores `self.max_segment_spans`, but the check in `_load_segment_data` was removed and `add-buffer.lua` hardcodes the limit to `1000`. Custom `max_segment_spans` values passed to `SpansBuffer` are silently ignored.
